I only played the single player game, and yes it's about time that I finally played through this wonderful single player campaign.  The graphics engine that DICE created for this game way back almost 8 years ago still looks great, until you get close up to walls or other materials.  The game was smooth, it was entertaining, it looked great, the smoke from the gun fire and explosions really played well into making the gun fights challenging when under heavy fire.  Your squad does help, but mostly it's up to you to make it all happen.

There are a variety of weapons though you can only carry two at a time.  I found my automatic rifle and my sniper rifle to be the best two to carry.  The storyline had its moments, though nothing to really brag about.  I did enjoy those moments of humanity during the war segments.  Some came off as cheesy, but others really were well directed and written.  I especially liked the helicopter hippy, great character.

The sound I found to be excellent.  The echo in a room with my shell cassings dropping compared to the sound it makes when you are outside was fantastic.  Overall sound was top notch as was the music when it came on.

The single player campaign was short, but maybe if it was longer I wouldn't have enjoyed it as much as it wasn't altogether that repetitive other than the gunfights which were welcomed each and every time.  The game is split between vehicle segments where you control the vehicle and gun, rail segments where you fly or drive but only get to control a gun, and then of course the on foot segments with the aforementioned gun fights.

DICE hasn't never truly let me down, and this game continues their standard of games.

Had I played this game many years, I would have played the multiplayer.  I tried getting on a Vietnam MP map and I was the sole soldier....I still died though.

I bought this game with the Vietnam DLC because I had fond memories of playing this back in a friends Xbox. However it turns out that you can't play it if you try to log in to your EA account via the game (through steam). Steam simply does not provide you with a key for the base game, only for the DLC... as that currently stands it creates huge issues.

If you absolutely want to buy this game via Steam follow this:

1) Create an Origin account if you haven't already
2) Synchronize your Steam and Origin accounts (You must go to https://help.ea.com/en and press log in). Note: On the area for entering the Username and Password prompt you will see a small button for Steam, use that.
3) Buy the game via Steam (doing it via origin will save you a lot of trouble). If you bought the DLC as well you will get a key for that, but not for the base game.
4) Go to https://help.ea.com/en/contact-us/?product=origin&platform=pc&category=manage-my-account&issue=hacked-account&isLoginForm=true&isContactForm=true and create a case, select chat option.
5) Tell them you bought game through steam and that you weren't provided with a base game key. They will require proof of purchase: https://help.ea.com/en/help/account/how-to-provide-proof-of-purchase/ 
6) EA support will add the game to your Origin Library. 
7) If you have DLC feel free to redeem that key via Origin. 

Hope this helps some of you to not go on a wild goose chase like i did the past 48 hours. Its insane how Steam won't provide support for this considering so many people have this issue. (Though i did notice some people were refunded after they complained).  EA is aware of the issue and will quickly help you, if you manage to skip their forums and find the live chat support.

On to the review part: Do I like this game? Yeah sure, its an older game but it checks out. Do I recommend buying it via Steam, hell no!

The community keeps telling everyone how this is the best battlefield game...

there's a reason for this, the reason is because its the best battlefield game,

graphics are still passable in 2018, despite being only marginally better than bf2 and worse than bf3.... its still "not bad" looking. 

gunplay has a crisp accurate feel to it not slowed down by pointless animation lag, movement and aiming is more like counter-strike or quake... direct movement, instead of the slower more sluggish (and yeah probably more realistic) movement you get in newer battlefield games. this crisp sharp aiming and movement is only helped by the several hundred FPS possible with a half decent GPU, 

servers are still alive and well despite it being a nearly 10 year old game, ignore the searchable servers online google will probably not show any active servers, support for this was removed a while ago when EA dropped official support... you can no longer find servers on game'tracker and other such sites. In game i see dozens of servers with active players with pings ranging from 20ms to 700ms... meaning (at a guess) there are still active servers all over the world.

netcode is sometimes a little janky and ingame ping does NOT show accurately, I live in the UK near to a server i play on a LOT.... the server in question is hosted in the UK but i get a 70ms ping in game... with a fibre connection... it should be maybe 10... 
 but its bad netcode and occasional lag is helped by everyone having the same advantage / disadvantage.... sometimes you die behind a wall when theres no way you were still visible... but sometimes THEY were behind a wall... its swings and roundabouts. 

audio is better than most of the later battlefield games in nearly all situations. in fact I would go so far as to call the audio "perfect", players emit barks when spotting which can give away your position, walking makes you quiet, running makes you louder, ect..

vehicles are not overpowered meaning infantry can pretty easily take out a badly prepared tank (2 c4 does the job)

map design is nice with a mix of close quarters battles and long range open maps. 

single player is the best of the series, with actual characters instead of blank slates that newer games have.

multiplayer is simply perfect... mostly because of the highly refined gunplay, awesome audio. amazing destruction, and nicely balanced weapons. the spotting system is as good as its ever been. there arent hundreds of unlockable weapon attachments there are around 20.... for all weapons.... this means its not a grindfest to unlock a decent weapon loadout like bf3 or 4. also there are 50x XP servers for people just wanting to unlock loadouts without spending a week or two at it. 
the skill ceiling in this game is as high as the skill ceiling in counterstrike... a new player can have a lot of fun but then you could spend hundreds of hours mastering it. 

a tip for new players.... never stop moving.... you will die with 1 headshot and a skilled player can make those while youre running anyway. 

generally its simply the best battlefield game so far, and its well worth the price especially on sale.

[b]There was a time when EA kept its games locked away on Origin, refusing to share its masterpieces beyond its own ecosystem. Battlefield: Bad Company 2 was one of the few rare exceptions, bridging the gap between EA and Steam when such a thing seemed impossible. Now, years later, EA has transitioned to its EA Platform, making its games more accessible. But regardless of the platform wars, one thing remains true, this game is a masterpiece.[/b]

[h1]A Battlefield Experience Like No Other[/h1]
[b]Unlike the more serious tone of other Battlefield games, Bad Company 2 stands out with its unforgettable characters, intense destruction, and fast-paced gameplay. The story campaign, while not the longest, delivers great humor, camaraderie, and explosive action, making it one of the best single-player experiences in the series.
And then, there's the multiplayer, where the game truly shines. Rush mode, the destructible environments, the chaotic vehicle battles, every match feels fresh and exciting. Even today, no other FPS quite captures the feeling of blowing up an entire building just to eliminate an enemy squad.[/b]

[h1]The Platform War: Steam vs. EA[/h1]
[b]When this review was originally written, EA was strictly separate, keeping its games locked to Origin. Bad Company 2 was one of the rare games that bridged that gap, allowing both Steam and EA players to experience its brilliance.
Now, with EA shifting to its new EA Platform, things have changed. The battle between platforms may continue, but one thing remains true, this game is legendary, no matter where you play it.[/b]

[h1]Pros:[/h1]
[list]
[*]Incredible destruction mechanics: Few FPS games match its level of environmental chaos.
[*]Memorable single-player campaign: The Bad Company squad is hilarious and engaging.
[*]Classic Battlefield-style multiplayer: Huge maps, vehicles, teamwork, and non-stop action.
[*]Rush mode remains one of the best FPS modes ever created.
[*]Still playable and enjoyable today: A testament to its quality and timeless gameplay.
[/list]
[h1]Cons:[/h1]
[list]
[*]Servers are not as populated as before: Finding full lobbies can be tough.
[*]Campaign is relatively short: Leaves you wanting more of Bad Company's squad.
[*]EA’s platform changes over the years: Originally tied to Origin, now EA Platform.
[/list]
[h1]Conclusion: A Battlefield Legend[/h1]
[b]No matter how much time passes, Battlefield: Bad Company 2 remains one of the greatest FPS games ever made. It’s a game that broke boundaries, not just in destruction and multiplayer innovation, but also in bridging EA and Steam when it seemed impossible.
If you’ve never played this game before, do yourself a favor and experience one of Battlefield’s finest moments.
May the best platform win, but Bad Company 2 remains a winner no matter where you play it. Highly Recommended![/b]

9 years ago, I got bored one humid afternoon and wandered into my older brothers room, playing the demo to a new shooter on his PS3. I inquired what the game was and he simply responded with two words "Bad Company". It wasn't a name that was familiar to me but the moment my older brother blew out the walls of a house with a grenade and leapt into the street moments before the damn thing came tumbling down in completely unscripted glory, I fell in love.

And of course, it never got a PC release!

Fast forward several years later, Bad Company 2 gets the PC release it deserved. And oh boy, is it a hell of a time!

The game takes place in an alternate future where Russia went full commie and decided to invade the rest of the globe in the vain of Modern Warfare 3. Except unlike MW3's nigh infinite resources to take over the globe, the ruskies in BC2 have an EMP ace up their sleeve in the vain of a super weapon that can knock out their enemies power-grids in one fell swoop.

And unfortunately for the rest of the globe, our heroes of the day are a ragtag group of ne're do wells, fuck ups and total idiots.

Bad Company was always the Black Sheep of the AAA Modern Military Genre with it's sense of humor and characters that I think stand out even more today, given the surge of gritty military shooters that have come out in the last 7 years. They are flawed, full of piss and vinegar and spout humor and character development instead of angst and cigar-chomping rage. And l loved ever second of their banter. Many times they would break out into spontanious conversations that honestly feel very natural and on-the-fly, almost like they got the VA's to stay in character while they just talked about a wide range of topics that are quite enjoyable to listen to!

Of course, great characters don't make for a particularly great game if the gameplay aspect sucks, thankfully, that's not the case!

Everything in the environment, from the buildings down to the terrain itself can be deformed with explosives and ripped appart with gunfire, hell, you can deforest an entire span of a river if you had enough grenades! Coupled with meaty gunplay, a wide range of weapons and astounding sound design, firefights are engaging and pretty damn tough! 

My complaints however are minimal. Ammo is rarely an issue with resupply crates every ten feet and the campaign is very linear despite more opportunities to branch off the path compared to other AAA shooters at the time and even today. The best mission takes place in a desert where you can drive and explore to your hearts content. Maybe DICE was strapped for time and could only make one large open map?

Of course, most folks migrate to the multiplayer once the campaign is over but for someone like me who adores Singleplayer campaigns, BC2 was a real treat and is perhaps the best Battlefield Campaign to date!

Those who are looking for the multiplayer component may be turned off by the smaller number of players compared to it's hayday but those looking for an explosive campaign will certainly find a lot of fun in the Campaign on offer! Give it a shot, it's the only Battlefield game on Steam after all! Might as well be the best!

Here's hoping we get a Bad Company 3! :)

Battlefield: Bad Company 2 is a team-based MMOFPS capture-the-checkpoint game based on massive maps. As you may have known, its sucessors are having a huge sucess. Battlefield easily became one of the iconic PC FPS game beside CoD and CSGO. BF: BC2 seriously blew my mind on both gameplay and graphics quality. As a 2010 game, I did not expect much from it. I got this on a massive sale and grabbed a few copies to send to my friends. I tested 3-4 levels of the SP and had some MP matches with my groupmates. Here are the pros and cons I pulled from it:

Pros:
+ Amazing optimization and graphics quality. Similar to its successors, this game is highly optimized. This means you can run BF games on bottleneck PCs with 60 fps. Graphics quality that is offered with this level of minimum specs are also amazing.
+ Classic Battlefield unforgiving & challenging shooting recoil. You can't point-and-shoot with laser-pinpoint accuracy like *cough*Call of Duty*cough*
+ Again, similar to its successors, the gameplay keeps a great balance between realism and entertaining arcade system. You can't run around no-scoping people with sniper rifles, but you sure won't get killed with 1 body shot like in Arma 3.
+ Servers & community are still active, most of them has x15 XP so you can rank up very quickly to unlock the weapons. A lot of people are still playing this game.
+ Bullet drop already exists, not as harsh as BF4 but it poses a challenge to snipers.
+ Tons of weapon choices
+ Steep, but enjoyable learning curve. Not as harsh as CSGO and not as lean as Call of Duty.
+ Definitely fun to play with your friends. Get them into a squad, turn your voice chat on, and go have a blast.
+ Perfect game to test the Battlefield experience. If you're afraid your money will go to waste on BF3/BF4/BFH/BF1, try this game first. Although the elements are very different, general gameplay is similar.
+ Haven't met any imperious server admins that enforces weird rules like in later BF games.
+ Classic BF destructible environment

Cons:
- Still K/D focused. Players are not really motivated to work with their team and solely focus on their own K/D. Players rarely bothers to capture a point and chose to sit on top of a hill with a sniper rifle instead. 
- Too many veteran players. Some people simply don't get bored with old games and they stay here for years. Arrogant veterans are squashing new players with helicopters/snipers.
- Base-raping is hardly controlled. Veteran players can easily find a sweet spot to camp the freshly spawned players. You basically will not have any chance to fight back if someone does this. Some servers kill these people but they often find loopholes to base-rape e.g. destroying freshly spawned vehicle
- I personally don't fancy the shooting. It's a bit wonky and awkward compared to other FPS games. I'm a 16-years FPS veteran that usually learns the pattern of new FPS games very quickly and can gain a headstart. In this particular game, it is very difficult for me to adapt.
- Adding friends seem to be very difficult in this game. It took me days and multiple tries to have my friend request sent to my groupmates

In conclusion, BF: BC2 is definitely worth it.  I wouldn't say that this game is better than its successors since I'm very meticulos with graphical quality and I despise downgrading games that I play. I would choose to play BF4/BF1 all day over BF: BC2.  However, this is an especially great game for people with bare-necessities PC specs or considering to purchase EA Origin's BF1/BF4/BFH. 

I hope my review can be helpful in your decision.

Thank you for reading!

Before I start with my review, I'd just like to shame EA for taking this game off the Steam store. In doing so, they are denying future generations the chance to experience an enjoyable campaign and a simple but fun Battlefield multiplayer. They are truly one of the worst gaming companies of all time, and I sincerely hope that their fate mirrors that of the Bad Company series. Anyway, let me get started on the game.

Bad Company 2, along with the first Battlefield Bad Company, have the best Battlefield campaigns by a country mile. There is simply no contest. Unlike the more recent Battlefield campaigns that have tried to emulate the more serious "tacticool" stories and gameplay of Call of Duty campaigns, the Bad Company series is humorous and light-hearted at its core. Whereas I couldn’t care less about most characters in a shooter, I found myself enjoying the back and forth between the main cast of Bad Company over the two games, even now when I’m much older. It reminds me a bit of the back-and-forth banter that I’d have with my friends in voice chat. It’s nice. The levels are usually quite large, some with a fair bit of travelling in a vehicle, so there’s plenty of time to listen to them talk. There’s plenty of destruction to be had in these levels too, because unlike the more modern Battlefields, almost everything is completely destructible in Bad Company 2. Entire villages can and will be flattened on the way to the objective.

The multiplayer in this Battlefield is very PS3/360 era console-esque. It's slower paced, smaller scale, lacks fixed wing aircraft, and has a larger emphasis on Rush Mode over the traditional Battlefield Conquest. Frankly the game is better for it. Sure, the gameplay feels a tad clunky compared to the slick feel of the modern Battlefield games, but that's what makes Bad Company 2 better than them. It's not all about running around like rabid greyhounds, sliding around corners and blasting opponents before they can even blink. Instead, there is time to think, and there is more than enough time to smell the roses - well before they get blown up anyway.
On top of this, the weapons are all meaty and feel solid to shoot. They are also loud, and the sound is impactful. The sound of bullets and explosions will echo around not just interiors but bounce off nearby buildings outside too. It’s a real joy to the ears.
There is one issue that I have with the online, and that is the weapon balancing, but it doesn't take away from the game or make me not want to play it. Far from it in-fact. Whenever I spend time on Bad Company 2, no matter how poorly I'm doing, I'm smiling and having a good time. There's just something so magic about this era of Battlefield that has been lost since the release of Battlefield 3. 

I'm also going to mention the Vietnam DLC in this review because it seems that it's no longer possible to review it separately. It is hands down one of the finest pieces of DLC that I have ever seen for a game. The maps, the vehicles, the weapons, and the music - wow, the music - it all came together to make it feel like a whole new game, and I believe for only £9.99 back in the day on the PS3. Contrast this with today where Battlefield games will drop pig slop maps once a quarter and sell skins for a tenner a piece. It’s not even comparable when you think about it. The standards for DLC have dropped significantly.

EA, do us all a favour and remaster Bad Company 1, Bad Company 2, and BF 1943. Then release them all on Steam. It won't take away from your modern CODified Battlefield games like BF6, but rather it will give us Bad Company era fans a chance to relive our memories. I'd sooner spend £70+ to fight in Harvest Day, Valparaiso, and Wake Island over spending a second longer in New Slop City.

The game puts the player into a mission that is set in 1944 in which you and your team infiltrate an island in the Sea of Japan to extract a Japanese scientist. Just last month played the campaign for Battlefield 1. It was bad and nothing of value would be lost, if Dice outright stopped making campaigns anymore.

As a palette cleanser and to see if nostalgia is tricking me, I replayed Bad Company 2. Probably me knowing what to do and how to play effectively, this third time was over faster than I expected. Still a respectable length though.

Conclusion. There were no rose-tinted glasses. Bad Company 2 just is the best and most fun Battlefield campaign. The level design is great. Characters and writing are extraordinarily memorable and likeable. Despite having a modern military setting, it works so well that the game goes full ham and jokes. Weapons are fun to play with but customization isn't much in your hands. At least there are frequent opportunities to change up your loadout.

The story is simple, yet timeless. A rag-tag group of military misfits, the Bad Company, somehow ends up in charge of retrieving a secret super weapon and prevent the invasion of USA by Russians. It's full of cliches but never feels trite because it knows how dumb it is and thus uses it as a strength to create an enjoyable story. That will take you across a varied range of locales, all with a unique feel and atmosphere. The occasional change of pace whether it's a vehicle mission, on-rails segment or mini-boss prevents monotony.

Gameplay is simply awesome. Weapon feedback, sounds and enemy behaviour is a joy. I can't stress how much more fun it is to play BC2 than BF3/4/1. It's sad and I expect BF5's and future Battlefield campaigns to be similarly awful. It's not only the story and writing either, as I said. BC2 has a mixture of graphical effects and clarity that has been long lost in newer BF games. Feels like in pursuit of visual bombast, Dice has either forgotten or forsaken a pleasing player experience. Explosions and other actions leave the screen filled with noise. On the other hand, BC2 never complicates an easy-for-the-eyes presentation while still offering a spectacular action presentation.

Not all is great, however. Technical issues are a remnant of Dice's last-gen transition back to PC and the settings and support are pretty basic, to say the least. Overdone Bloom you could kill a person with, no ultra-widescreen support, no FOV slider or in-depth control over visual settings made it a bit cumbersome to set up properly, but once you get the Widescreen fixer app, it's smooth sailing apart cutscenes not looking right at times due to an increased FOV. You can toggle it on the fly with a hotkey, so it's OK.

It's really the mix of all the good parts that make Bad Company 2 stand the test of time. Dice's continuous fumbles make me believe it was due to stars aligning rather than intentional brilliance. Every fan of first-person shooters needs to play this at least once.
The golden age of Battlefield, they'll never again reach this level of quality and fun. Shame DICE and EA are determined to take a steaming dump on it and the franchise.
